key_insight: Finite-energy bosonic codes let a single oscillator sense an external force while protecting an unknown logical qubit, with probe readout independent of the logical state.
engineering_relevance: The approach could combine force sensing and recoverable quantum memory in one superconducting oscillator.
method: Encode logical amplitudes across discrete wave-packet sites.
Store the force signal in a shared internal coordinate for endpoint readout.
Use binomial site recovery to correct logical errors and packet-dependent probe distortions.
evidence_signal: For a (2r+2)-packet code under photon loss γ, the abstract reports memory infidelity scaling as O(γ^(r+1)) and residual memory–probe correlations as O(γ^(r+2)), plus superconducting-circuit benchmarks.
watch_item: Photon-number dephasing and Kerr nonlinearity constrain encoding choices; the abstract does not report an experimental demonstration.
paper_title: Force Sensing in a Recoverable Bosonic Quantum Memory
